subject: Request: temporary throttle softening for planned simulation
messages:
From: Aidan Clarke <aidan.clarke@nomadhealth.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: Nomad Health Ops <ops@nomadhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary throttle softening request for planned staging simulation

Hi Rohan —

We have a large, time-boxed simulation scheduled in our staging environment next Thursday (Nov 5) to validate our batch inference pipeline ahead of a Q1 rollout. The test will replay ~120M tokens over a 6-hour window with two concentrated waves: a 45-minute ramp at 11:00–11:45 PT and a 30-minute peak at 14:00–14:30 PT.

Our current production config is within normal limits, but the staging run will exceed the standard per-minute token quota and the fairness-based throttles in the hosted API. We want to avoid false positives (errors/retries) during the replay and get consistent latency numbers.

Request: Can Redwood temporarily relax the rate limit/fairness throttle for our account for the Nov 5 window, or provide a short-term elevated token buffer for staging? We only need this for that single run — we’re happy to accept additional cost and any monitoring that comes with the change.

Useful details (attached nomad_simulation_window.csv):
- Total tokens: ~120,000,000 over 6 hours
- Expected qps: baseline 30 rps; two spikes up to ~650 requests/min for short bursts
- Allowed latency SLO: 500ms p95 (we do not expect to tolerate p99 > 1.5s)

If you need a signed amendment or a short-term addendum to our contract, tell me what you need and I’ll route to procurement.

Thanks — appreciate any options you can propose.

Best,
Aidan Clarke
Senior PM, Platform
Nomad Health
From: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
To: Aidan Clarke <aidan.clarke@nomadhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throttle softening request for planned staging simulation

Aidan —

Thanks for the heads-up and the CSV — that’s helpful. Short answer: we can support a scoped, temporary relaxation but we need a brief technical and operational plan so we don’t affect other tenants.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether the traffic originates from a single API key/service account or several?
2) Exact ramp pattern (per-minute or per-second series) — the CSV helped, but we need a second-by-second bucket for the peak 45-min ramp and the 30-min peak.
3) Are you able to implement exponential backoff on the client for any 429s during the simulation? That helps us avoid cascading retries.

Proposal (quick):
- 6-hour window with two scoped adjustments: a modest token-buffer increase for the whole window and a higher short-window limit for the two peak bursts.
- Canary phase: enable the elevated limits for a 30-minute canary at the lower peak, observe telemetry for 30–60 minutes, then open the full window if healthy.
- Cost: we’ll provide an estimate; you can choose to accept usage charges for overage.

Operational notes: we’ll need se-ingest and the routing team to pin your requests to a compatible capacity lane; that could incur a transient tolerance hit if capacity is constrained. If you can sign off on a canary, I’ll pull Marissa in to draft the exact config and a short amendment.

Are you available for a 20-min call Monday to finalize? Otherwise reply with the requested details and I’ll circulate the config.

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com, Aidan Clarke <aidan.clarke@nomadhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throttle softening request for planned staging simulation

Aidan / Rohan —

Looping in a suggested technical approach from SE/SRE perspective. I attached a short PDF (proposed_sla_change.pdf) with the exact knob changes and a cost sketch. Highlights below:

Planned config (per account):
- Baseline per-minute token quota: increase from 1,200,000 tokens/min to 2,500,000 tokens/min for the 6-hour window.
- Short-window peak policy: for the two bursts, allow a surge token pool of up to 6,000,000 tokens over any 15-minute sliding window, enforced by account-tagging.
- Fairness policy: temporarily relax distributed fairness for the tagged requests only; other accounts’ fairness unaffected. We’ll mark requests from your staging API key with a staging tag.
- Throttle behavior: keep 429s active but reduce early-termination thresholds; client backoff still required.

Canary plan:
- 30-min canary at the lower spike (~11:00 PT). Monitoring: token burn rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx/429 counts, and CPU/GPU slot contention.
- If p95 < 500ms and 429 < 0.5% during canary, proceed to full window. If not, revert and run a second canary after adjustments.

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: transient queueing on shared lanes if capacity tight. Mitigation: temporary traffic steering to a reserved capacity pool (we can reserve a small dedicated slot for the 6-hour window).

Cost estimate (rough): additional $9,200 — includes reserved capacity for the 6-hour window + overage token fees. Final numbers in attached PDF.

Attachments: proposed_sla_change.pdf (2 pages, config + cost), nomad_simulation_window.csv (original)

If that plan sounds OK to Nomad, I can open a short-term addendum and schedule the canary/run. Rohan — do you want me to draft the addendum and ops runbook?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aidan Clarke <aidan.clarke@nomadhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: Nomad Health Ops <ops@nomadhealth.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throttle softening request for planned staging simulation

Thanks, Marissa & Rohan — this looks good.

We accept the canary + staged window approach and will sign the short-term addendum. I confirmed the traffic will originate from a single staging API key (staging-nomad-01) and our client will implement backoff as requested.

Requested kickoff: Monday Nov 2, 10:30 PT to walk the team through the canary and confirm the addendum. I’ve looped our ops team.

I’ll approve the cost estimate with procurement as soon as we get the addendum draft. Deal id for our internal tracking: NH-2026-1147.

Best,
Aidan
Senior PM, Platform
Nomad Health
